assessment.nobel_worthiness: Horizon-scale imaging made a black-hole shadow an observable object and opened a striking new regime of gravitational astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: These names represent the theoretical proposal, the long-baseline interferometry leadership, and the effort that brought the global array and imaging result together; the achievement depended on a very large collaboration.
assessment.maturity: The M87* and Sagittarius A* results provide powerful confirmation, while continued observations and improved imaging can refine the interpretation.
uncertainties: How to recognize the decisive individual contributions within a worldwide collaboration remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube established high-energy neutrinos as a new observational channel for the Universe, a major advance in astroparticle physics.
assessment.attribution: Halzen's scientific leadership and Karle's central role in the detector and collaboration make a strong case, though the discovery was built by a large international team.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse astrophysical flux is firmly established; source identification is progressing and will determine how far this window can take us.
uncertainties: The origin of most of the measured neutrino flux is still unresolved.
Individual credit is challenging for a large detector collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson completed a central part of the Standard Model and required extraordinary detectors and analysis.
assessment.attribution: The named leaders represent ATLAS and CMS contributions, but the discovery is inseparable from thousands of collaborators; any individual selection is necessarily incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The particle and its properties have been confirmed over many years of measurements, making the discovery exceptionally mature.
uncertainties: The main uncertainty is fair recognition of the collective experimental work within a prize that can name only a few people.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision maps of the microwave background revealed the acoustic structure of the early Universe and established a quantitative foundation for modern cosmology.
assessment.attribution: These names span major observational and theoretical contributions, although the achievement drew on several missions and broad international teams.
assessment.maturity: Independent measurements and decades of consistency with cosmological observations make the core result highly mature.
uncertainties: The discovery is a sequence of contributions, so the boundaries of the prize-worthy advance and the individuals central to it need careful definition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Connecting neutron-star mergers to heavy-element production united gravitational-wave, electromagnetic, and nuclear astrophysics in a landmark result.
assessment.attribution: The proposed names represent key theoretical and modeling contributions; the observational discovery itself involved extensive teams across multiple facilities.
assessment.maturity: The 2017 multi-messenger event gave compelling support, but the relative contribution of mergers to the cosmic r-process inventory remains under study.
uncertainties: The result is still developing, and the full population of r-process sites is not settled.
Credit spans predictions, modeling, and large observational collaborations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks transformed precision timekeeping and enable tests of fundamental physics through unprecedented control of atomic transitions.
assessment.attribution: Katori and Ye are clearly associated with the key independent approaches and their experimental realization.
assessment.maturity: The clocks are now highly developed and independently replicated, with continuing improvements in accuracy and applications.
uncertainties: Whether the central achievement should be recognized now or after a further landmark redefinition of the second is a matter of timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fast radio bursts revealed an unexpected class of energetic cosmic transients and created a productive new field of radio astronomy.
assessment.attribution: The discovery team is identifiable and the credited names reflect the observation and its early analysis.
assessment.maturity: The phenomenon is well established and repeating sources have broadened the field, but the population and physical mechanisms remain unsettled.
uncertainties: The long-term physical significance of FRBs is not yet clear enough to judge the full scale of the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Laser-plasma wakefield acceleration is a bold route to compact accelerators and has enabled important experimental progress.
assessment.attribution: These names represent the foundational concept and major experimental development, though many groups have advanced the field.
assessment.maturity: The acceleration principle is established, but reliable, high-quality beams and broad scientific use remain active challenges.
uncertainties: The Nobel-scale impact will depend on whether the technique becomes a dependable accelerator platform or enables a distinctive discovery.
